messages.subject: cluster size?
parts:
All,

We are having some discussions on what designates a cluster. Should 2 =
(or more) birds associating in a flock be considered and analyzed as a =
cluster, even if each one is detected independently (i.e., each one =
vocalized, revealing it's presence independently of the other)? =20

Thank you,

messages.author: 5140016d70f6ba82
messages.subject: Re: cluster size?
parts:
This is a difficult problem because it can be viewed as either dependent
detections or underestimating group size. It is important to recognize
that a group for distance sampling may not be a group from a biological
stand point. As I view it, a "group" is a collection of animals that
are sighted together. If as you describe, birds are detected
independently even though they are in close proximity, I would treat
them as separate observations. Then I would also explore a bootstrap
variance approach to guard against underestimating the variance due to
dependence in detections.

Any other thoughts out there?

--jeff
